requirement:
`Criterion::execute` can compute an answer without a configured model provider.
A criterion can compute its answer directly using tracked inputs; deterministic
execution needs no configured agent.
rationale:
The requirement has two obligations. `Criterion::execute` can compute an answer without a configured model provider. A criterion can compute that answer directly from tracked inputs.

- **No agent configured:** `crates/trust-but-verify/src/agent/tests.rs#fn[deterministic_validation_uses_required_storage_without_an_agent]` builds a `Validator::new(graph)` with no agent. It runs a deterministic `Review` criterion whose `execute` reads the node text through `ctx.read`. It asserts that `result.output().rationale` equals the node text, so the answer comes from the tracked read. It also stores the evidence and asserts that the saved dependency is `Dependency::Node(Node(1), fingerprint)` with the expected fingerprint value, so the read was tracked.
- **Provider setup errors do not affect deterministic criteria:** `crates/trust-but-verify/src/agent/configured.rs#mod[tests]/fn[configured_agents_initialize_only_when_asked_and_report_setup_errors]` configures an agent with a deliberately missing credential. A deterministic `refresh_evidence` of `Question(false)` still succeeds, with output false and one dependency. Only the `verify(Question(true))` call that asks the agent fails, with `ValidationError::Agent` naming the missing credential. This shows that a bad provider configuration does not block deterministic computation. It also shows the provider is not initialized unless asked.
- **Further coverage:**
  - `crates/trust-but-verify/src/graph/validation_tests.rs#fn[caller_reuses_negative_answers_and_compares_revisions_explicitly]` and `crates/trust-but-verify/tests/contracts.rs#fn[criteria_keep_typed_answers_and_persist_only_when_requested]` also run deterministic criteria through `Validator::new` with no agent. They check the answers, the dependency lists and the read and execution counts.
  - Across these tests, criteria that read tracked inputs and criteria that read none (empty dependencies) both compute outputs without a provider.

The tests cover both the no-provider case and the tracked-input case, and they assert the outcomes. I found no gap.
